in_text_mentions: Brain MR images of our case are presented in Figures 1, 2, 3, and 4. Our patient is a 42-year-old Japanese man who first developed hand tremor in his middle teens. He noticed his right foot dragging at age 35, and generalized hypotonia, hyperextensibility, aphonia, micrographia, hyperreflexia, dystonia of his face, and cognitive impairment at age 42. Rigidity, spasticity, and chorea were not observed. His deceased mother had presented similar symptoms. His serum ferritin concentration was apparently low. He was tested by means of the molecular technique and diagnosed as having neuroferritinopa

All images presented here were taken with a 1.5 Tesla MR System. T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and T2*-weighted sequences were collected in the transverse plane. A T1-weighted image is useful for evaluating the atrophy and size of a cyst. As compared with the image at 35 years (Figure 1), that at 42 years demonstrates progression of the cystic formation and deterioration of the cortical atrophy in the frontal lobes (Figures 2(c) and 3(c)). Cortical atrophy can also be seen in the cerebellum (Figure 2(a)). Enlargement of the lateral ventricles is evident (Figure 2(d)).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: H&E section of putamen from a patient with hereditary ferritinopathy (neuroferritinopathy) showing the disease's hallmark ferritin inclusion bodies; human patient histopathology directly attributable to the configured disease. B: Perls' Prussian blue iron stain of putamen from the same hereditary ferritinopathy patient, demonstrating iron deposits associated with ferritin inclusion bodies; the vocabulary's iron-deposition key is MRI-specific, so the histology iron finding is proposed. C: Immunohistochemistry with mutant FTL antibody labeling ferritin inclusion bodies in putamen of a hereditary ferritinopathy patient; direct disease-specific human patient histology. D: Immunohistochemistry with wild-type FTL antibody labeling ferritin inclusion bodies in putamen of a hereditary ferritinopathy patient; direct disease-specific human patient histology. E: Ubiquitin immunohistochemistry confirming ubiquitinated ferritin inclusion...

panels.figure_caption: Inclusion bodies, iron deposits, and immunohistochemistry from a patient with hereditary ferritinopathy. Sections of putamen show numerous ferritin IBs of various sizes (A–E), which are ubiquitinated (E). Ferritin IBs were also present in neurons and glial cells of the cerebellum (F). Hematoxylin and eosin (A); Perls' Prusian blue method for iron (B); and immunohistochemistry using antibodies against mutant FTL (C), wild-type FTL (D), ubiquitin (E), and FTH1 (F). Scale bars: (A–F), 50 μm.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (a, b, c, d, e). a: T1-weighted axial MRI at the pontine level from a 42-year-old man diagnosed with neuroferritinopathy (article title 'MRI findings in neuroferritinopathy'); caption states cerebellar cortex atrophy. Real human patient MRI showing a described disease manifestation; atrophy is not in the vocabulary, so it is recorded as a proposed finding. b: T1-weighted axial MRI of the midbrain in the same neuroferritinopathy patient; caption describes hypointense change in the substantia nigra, representing brain iron accumulation. Substantia nigra is anatomically distinct from the basal ganglia, so it is recorded as a proposed finding rather than forcing the basal ganglia iron-deposition key. c: T1-weighted axial MRI at the basal ganglia level in the same neuroferritinopathy patient. Caption explicitly describes symmetrical hypointense signals in the caudate head and globus pallidus (iron deposition) and fan-shaped cystic change of the lenticular...
panels.attribution_text: Ohta and Takiyama. MRI findings in neuroferritinopathy.. Neurology research international 2012. doi:10.1155/2012/197438. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: T1-weighted images (TR 400 msec/ TE 9 msec) of the same patient at 42 years of age. (a) A cross-section at the pontine level shows cerebellar cortex atrophy. (b) An image of a midbrain section demonstrates the hypointense change in the substantia nigra. (c) An image at the level of the basal ganglia shows symmetrical hypointense signals in the head of the caudate nucleus and globus pallidus. As compared with the findings at 35 years, the hypointense signals in the pallidum extend to the putamen. The cystic changes of the lenticular nuclei can be clearly observed. The shape of the cyst is fan shaped and exactly fits the region of the lenticular nucleus. The cerebral cortex in the frontal lobes is atrophic. The hypointense lesion in the caudate head observed in the image at 35 years of age seems to be combined with the hypointense signal of the anterior horn of the lateral ventricle. (d) In this image, enlargement of the lateral ventricles is evident. (e) This image shows cerebral cortical atrophy.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: T2*-weighted gradient-echo MRI of the same 42-year-old neuroferritinopathy patient; caption describes signal loss with central hyperintense lesions in the dentate nucleus, a recognized iron-deposition finding in neuroferritinopathy. B: T2* midbrain image of the same neuroferritinopathy patient showing hypointense change in the red nucleus, consistent with brain iron deposition. C: T2* image showing cystic degeneration of the basal ganglia with peripheral signal loss (iron) and bilateral thalamic abnormalities; classic neuroferritinopathy MRI features directly captioned. D: Real patient T2* MRI section at the central lateral ventricle level from the same neuroferritinopathy figure; caption names the anatomical level but no specific abnormality is described, so included as part of the diagnostic figure with lower confidence. E: T2* image of the same neuroferritinopathy patient showing iron deposition in the cerebral cortex detected...
panels.attribution_text: Ohta and Takiyama. MRI findings in neuroferritinopathy.. Neurology research international 2012. doi:10.1155/2012/197438. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: T2*-weighted images (TR 400 msec/ TE 25 msec) obtained with a gradient echo sequence in the same patient at 42 years old. (a) A cross-section at the pontine level. The signal loss with central hyperintense lesions in the dentate nucleus is more obvious than that observed on T2WI. (b) An image of the midbrain demonstrates the hypointense change in the red nucleus. (c) Cystic degeneration of the basal ganglia with a rim of peripheral signal loss is obvious. In the thalamus, bilateral hyperintense abnormalities surrounded by slight hypointensity can be seen. (d) An image of a section of the central part of the lateral ventricles. (e) The iron deposition in the cerebral cortex is detected as signal loss.
